title: Angle Bisector Between Two Lines — The a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ Rule
notes: **Normalized distance.** Dividing aᵢx + bᵢy + cᵢ by √(aᵢ² + bᵢ²) turns its absolute value into the perpendicular distance from (x, y) to that line; equating the two distances gives the bisector locus.

**Sign convention.** First rewrite both equations so c₁ and c₂ are positive. The bisector containing the origin then takes the (+) sign in (a₁x + b₁y + c₁)/√(a₁² + b₁²) = ± (a₂x + b₂y + c₂)/√(a₂² + b₂²).

**Acute vs obtuse.** If a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ < 0 the (+) bisector is acute; if a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ > 0 the (+) bisector is obtuse. When the product is zero the lines are perpendicular and both bisectors are equally inclined.
**Perpendicularity check.** The two bisectors are always at right angles, so their slopes satisfy m₁m₂ = −1; use this to verify the simplified equations.
**Worked step.** Expand each normalized equation with the chosen sign, collect x and y terms, and simplify — the constant ratio, not the raw coefficients, decides which bisector is acute.
topicTitle: Angle Bisector Between Two Lines — The a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ Rule
summary: The acute/obtuse bisector of two lines is selected by the sign of a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ once the constant terms are made positive.
